defects: hv_nontrivial (`∃ x, v i x ≠ 0`) is vacuously true for every absolute value (since v i x ≠ 0 whenever x ≠ 0 always), so it fails to express the 'nontrivial absolute value' condition (v i not equal to the trivial/discrete absolute value) required by the informal statement and gold's IsNontrivial

hv_inequiv (`v i ≠ v j` as functions) is strictly weaker than gold's `¬(v i).IsEquiv (v j)`; two distinct absolute values can still be equivalent (induce the same topology, e.g. v and v^c), so this hypothesis fails to guarantee the pairwise topological inequivalence the theorem actually needs

The added `[TopologicalSpace F]` instance on F is disconnected from v: the codomain of the DenseRange map is `ι → F` under this single fixed topology (repeated via the product), not the per-index topology WithAbs (v i) induced by each absolute value v i, so the conclusion does not capture density with respect to the v_i-induced topologies at all

Conclusion uses a bare lambda `fun x i => x` into `ι → F` instead of algebraMap into the dependent product `(i : ι) → WithAbs (v i)`, losing the essential per-factor topological structure from the informal statement
Fintype ι used instead of Finite ι (minor, largely interchangeable, but still a deviation)
